# Styling

Our react components consume the styles from the `@airbus/styles` package **at runtime**<br />
For more details, see https://github.airbus.corp/Airbus/design-system/blob/develop/packages/styles/README.md

## Global styles

Very minimalistic global styles are included.<br />
Target the `body` element if you want these styles everywhere, or apply the styles locally on any element.<br />
It will affect all child elements of the target.

See [CSS Baseline](https://css.design-system.airbus.corp/?path=/docs/general-visual-styles-baseline) for details.

```html
<div className="ds-styles">
  <h1>Heading 1</h1>
</div>
```

## Dark Mode

Complete support for dark mode is available from v3. This allows the application built using design system to support dark mode holistically and selectively as well.

Here is how to use dark mode

```js
import React from "react";
import ReactDOM from "react-dom";
import { Button, ColorModeProvider } from "@airbus/components-react";

function App() {
  return (
    <ColorModeProvider mode="dark">
      <Button variant="primary">Button</Button>
    </ColorModeProvider>
  );
}

ReactDOM.render(<App />, document.querySelector("#app"));
```

Official background color for dark mode is <code>#111111</code> For the purpose of demo, we have applied this background color in all the examples involving dark mode.

```css
.bg-dark { 
  background-color: #111111; 
}
.p-1 { 
  padding: 1rem; 
}
```


## Themes

We support Airbus and Skywise themes.<br />
Airbus Design System components are self-supporting, they will inject and use the Airbus branded theme by default.

Here is how to use the skywise branded theme

```js
import React from "react";
import ReactDOM from "react-dom";
import { Button, ThemeProvider } from "@airbus/components-react";

function App() {
  return (
    <ThemeProvider brand="skywise">
      <Button variant="primary">I'm a skywise primary button</Button>
    </ThemeProvider>
  );
}

ReactDOM.render(<App />, document.querySelector("#app"));
```

## Overriding styles

We don't force you to use any particular approach for styling your application.<br />
You can adopt CSSinJS with [styled-components](https://styled-components.com/), [emotion](https://emotion.sh/), etc.<br />
Or you can choose another solution like [sass](https://sass-lang.com/), [tailwind](https://tailwindcss.com/), etc.

### Styled-Components

Add [styled-components](https://styled-components.com/) to your project : `npm install styled-components --save`

```js
import styled from "styled-components";

const CustomButton = styled(Button)`
  border: 2px dashed #000;
`;
```

### Vanilla styles

Global class names

```css
.CustomButton {
  padding: 20px;
}
```

```js
import './CustomButton.css';

export const CustomButton = () => {
  return (
    <Button className="CustomButton">Custom Button</Button>
  );
}
```

Inline styles

```js
export const CustomButton = () => {
  return (
    <Button style={{ border: "2px dashed #000" }}>Custom Button</Button>
  );
}
```
